United States: Labor Department Proposes Sweeping Changes to PERM Program
news.og_title: Labor Department Proposes Sweeping Changes to PERM Program
news.og_desc:
•	The proposed regulation would substantially revise the PERM labor certification process by broadening the Department of Labor’s adjudication and enforcement authority and imposing significant new employer obligations. 
•	The Department of Labor (DOL) is proposing major changes to PERM recruitment rules, including eliminating current print ad requirements, mandating standard recruitment steps for nearly all PERM positions, lengthening the required recruitment period to a minimum of 90 days, requiring submission of recruitment materials with the application, and generally requiring PERM recruitment to mirror or exceed the employer’s normal methods for non-PERM recruitment.
•	DOL also proposes to prohibit PERM filings if the employer has had a layoff in the same or a similar occupation in the same area of intended employment within the past two years. It also institutes a layoff notice requirement even beyond the filing date of the PERM application. 
•	DOL is also seeking to eliminate Schedule A, which currently exempts professional nurses, physical therapists, and foreign nationals of exceptional ability from the PERM recruitment process.
•	DOL will accept public feedback on the proposal for 60 days after the rule is formally published tomorrow. The proposed revisions to the PERM program would not take effect until the regulation clears the federal rulemaking process and is finalized, which typically takes several months.
